quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should drivers stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at the driver.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian cross. You may go only after the crosswalk is completely clear.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the brake.
Hold the steering wheel firm and brake gently.
Pull over fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firm and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light braking. Do not stop on the road. Pull to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: One solid yellow line and one broken yellow line mark the center of the road. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no cars are coming toward you.
You can only make right turns here.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no cars are coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to finish crossing.
Go around them to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: In bad weather or low light, your headlights should be set to:

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams bounce off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rainy or foggy weather. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Loss of vehicle control.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of vehicle control.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your car and ride smoothly. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: On a road with multiple lanes, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a dashed line, only drivers on the dashed side can cross the center line to pass. Drivers on the solid side cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: A railroad crossing ahead.
A pedestrian crossing ahead.
A no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about upcoming hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, you must attach a note with your name, phone number, and address to it.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you can go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You stop completely first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the right lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the right lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If your lane has a green arrow, you can go in that direction when it is safe. This is true even if the main light is red.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Brake gently and gradually so your car stops smoothly.

questions.question: You have a minor crash with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your car in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your car out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your car for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a minor crash with no injuries, move your car out of traffic if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your car, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bike.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bikes are unpredictable and often change direction suddenly. Children and bikes are small and hard to see, so stay alert.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Pull completely off the road if possible.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull completely off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, get all four wheels off the road if you can.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use low beam headlights in fog. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. They mean you cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What lights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back and create glare, making it hard to see.

questions.question: What should a driver always do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Never assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always watch the situation at intersections. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: What do blue signs tell you about?

options.text: Services for drivers.
Construction and maintenance.
Distance to locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Services for drivers.
questions.explanation: Blue signs show where to find services like rest areas, food, or hospitals.

questions.question: Why signal while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to stop signaling before the turn is complete.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to stop signaling early.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, riders, and pedestrians what you are doing.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a freeway from an on-ramp?

options.text: You have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the freeway.
Force your way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Yield to traffic already on the freeway. Merge safely when you have space.

questions.question: When can you drive in an HOV lane?

options.text: When you are driving faster than traffic.
When you are driving slower than traffic.
When your vehicle has more than one person in it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle has more than one person in it.
questions.explanation: HOV lanes are for vehicles with multiple people. These lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot see clearly at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions.
questions.explanation: Stop at the intersection. Inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions before entering.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Increase the distance between your car and the one ahead. This gives you more time to stop if needed. Use headlights correctly, following high beam and low beam rules.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the brain first, reducing your judgment and ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
The car next to the broken line can pass.
The car next to the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car next to the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass.

questions.question: The car ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians cross.
Change lanes and pass the stopped car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians cross.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped car at a crosswalk. You may not see pedestrians crossing. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
